newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Marshall Islands seek aid to clean up N-test damage.
newsitem.headline: Marshall Islands seek aid to clean up N-test damage.

text.p: The Marshall Islands on Monday appealed for international assistance to deal with damage caused by nuclear tests after the Second World War, when it was part of a U.S.-administered U.N. Trust Territory.

The islands, which became fully self-governing in free association with the United States in 1990 and joined the United Nations in 1991, include Bikini and other atolls where early nuclear tests were conducted.

Addressing the General Assembly, Phillip Muller, the foreign minister of the Pacific Ocean nation, said his government had recently learned that "the damage caused by nuclear weapon test programmes during the Trusteeship are far greater and more horrible than that originally disclosed."

"As a result of all 67 nuclear weapon tests, the effect of radiation released is currently known to include more atolls and more groups of people than previously disclosed, as reported by the White House advisory committee on human radiation experiments."

Costs related to the effects of radiation "make it very hard to properly treat and care for the people who have, and continue to show, radiation-related illnesses. This also applies to programmes related to the rehabilitation of contaminated islands and the safe resettlement of affected communities," Muller said.

"We cannot solve these problems on our own and we feel obliged to appeal to the international community. Our concern continues to be that our situation has not been fully addressed and rectified up to now."

Muller welcomed what he called the "new willingness of the U.S. authorities to constructively work with" the islands to address the full range of outstanding nuclear issues. "We acknowledge the assistance which has been provided up to now, which includes efforts at cleanup and resettlement. But much more needs to be done," he said.
